newsitem.title: UK: LME copper volatile, firmer in late activity.
newsitem.headline: LME copper volatile, firmer in late activity.

text.p: London Metal Exchange three months copper extended an afternoon move up in late inter-office trading, after a day of volatile whipsaw trading, ahead of another expected drop in warehouse stocks.

Copper had fallen on Thursday as low as $1,902 per tonne on speculative selling after an early high at $1,930 reached on news that workers at Kennecott's Utah operations went on strike and plants were working at a reduced level.

Prices then ended the afternoon kerb towards the top of the range at $1,924 and copper was bid at $1,935 by the time Comex closed at 1800 GMT. Traders said stocks were expected to fall on Friday by 8,000-10,000 tonnes after declining by 10,950 tonnes on Tuesday.
Aluminium held the sharp gains of the day in late activity and was around the same value as it had been at the kerb close, at $1,369, by 1800 GMT.
